_comment: The Sources shelf: every work the app draws on or cites, one card each, so anyone can see what a source is, who made it, when, its license, and where to read or find it. atlas build reads this file (crates/atlas-cli/src/shelf.rs) with sources.json, the sources config/aramaic.json cites and the sites the questions in config/hard-verses.json link to (shown at Deep), and writes shelf.json for the Sources tab.
groups: the shelves, in the order shown. id: lowercase letters and hyphens, named by a work's group. name: the plain heading.

works: one card per work. id: unique, lowercase letters, digits and hyphens; a work that is a dataset uses its sources.json id. group: a groups id. plain: what the Simple level shows, the kind of work and when, in words anyone understands (48 characters at most), such as "Bible dictionary, 1897", or for a book or article what it is about, such as "Article on the word Abba, 1988". title. by: who wrote or made it. when: as shown, such as "1897" or "around AD 200". what: one or two plain, modest sentences (240 characters at most).

license: public-domain, cc-by-4.0, cc-by-sa-4.0, mit or copyrighted; licenseNote (optional) says more, such as a dataset's license beside its text's. The app ships only public domain, CC BY 4.0 and CC BY-SA 4.0 material, and the MIT-licensed word-meaning model Ask the Bible uses to tell which prepared question someone means. A copyrighted work is cited and linked, never quoted at length or stored.

datasets: the sources.json ids whose pinned files are this work; [] for a work the app only cites. Each sources.json id belongs to exactly one work. A dataset no work claims still gets a plain card made from sources.json, with a build warning.

read: where to read the whole work free, either {"app": "bible"} or {"app": "dictionary"} inside the app, or {"url", "label"} for a free full copy of that very work, checked by opening it. Never for a copyrighted work. find: {"url", "label"}, a link for the citation: https://doi.org/ and the DOI when there is one, else a publisher or library catalog page, else a WorldCat search. Required for a copyrighted work. Links are https only.

citation: the full bibliographic citation, shown at Deep. cites: parts of the source strings the app shows (config/aramaic.json sources, and the site of each read_more link in config/hard-verses.json) that name this work, each found where a word starts ("Bible.org" is not found in "STEPBible.org"). The build records where the app cites each work and warns about any source string no work matches. Keep each one long enough to match only this work's strings; plain ASCII is safest. onlyWhenCited: true for a work shown only while the app cites it, such as a website that only the hard passages at Deep and the "Often asked" answers link to. It needs cites and no datasets.

To add a work: add one entry with facts checked against the work itself, its publisher or a library catalog, never guessed; give it cites for each source string that names it; if it is a dataset, pin it in sources.json and credit it in NOTICE.md as well. Works only drafted in config/layers.json are added when they go live.

groups.name: Websites to read more on a verse

works.title: Berean Standard Bible (BSB)
works.by: The Berean Bible Translation Committee, with Bible Hub, Discovery Bible and OpenBible.com
works.what: A modern English translation from the Hebrew, Aramaic and Greek. It is the English the app opens in, with its own footnotes and section headings.
works.licenseNote: Dedicated to the public domain on 30 April 2023.
works.citation: The Holy Bible, Berean Standard Bible (BSB), produced in cooperation with Bible Hub, Discovery Bible, OpenBible.com and the Berean Bible Translation Committee (2016; dedicated to the public domain 30 April 2023), https://berean.bible/. Text via scrollmapper/bible_databases; footnotes and section headings via the USFM edition in usfm-bible/examples.bsb.

works.title: NET Bible (NET)
works.by: Biblical Studies Press, with more than 25 Bible scholars
works.what: A modern English translation from the Hebrew, Aramaic and Greek, made with thousands of translators' notes. Choose NET above the reader to read it; it is read live from the publisher and never stored.
works.licenseNote: Copyright Biblical Studies Press, L.L.C. Free apps and websites may quote it when each quotation ends with (NET) linked to netbible.org. The app reads it one chapter at a time and never stores it.
works.citation: The NET Bible®, New English Translation, copyright ©1996, 2019 by Biblical Studies Press, L.L.C., https://netbible.org. Scripture quoted by permission. All rights reserved. Read live from the publisher's web service, labs.bible.org.

works.title: King James Version (KJV)
works.by: Translators appointed under King James I; the 1769 Oxford text edited by Benjamin Blayney
works.what: The best-known older English Bible. The app never shows it: search uses its wording so a verse remembered in King James words is still found.
works.licenseNote: Public domain in most of the world; in the United Kingdom the Crown's rights in the KJV are managed by Cambridge University Press.
works.citation: The Holy Bible, King James Version (1611), Oxford standard text of 1769 (ed. Benjamin Blayney). Text via scrollmapper/bible_databases (public domain).

works.title: American Standard Version (ASV)
works.by: The American committee of the English Revised Version
works.what: An American revision of the King James Bible. The app never shows it: search uses its wording so a verse remembered in words close to the ASV is still found.
works.citation: The Holy Bible, American Standard Version (New York: Thomas Nelson & Sons, 1901). Text via scrollmapper/bible_databases (public domain).

works.plain: Hebrew Old Testament, word by word
works.title: Translators Amalgamated Hebrew OT (TAHOT)
works.by: STEPBible.org, based on work at Tyndale House, Cambridge
works.what: Every Hebrew and Aramaic word of the Old Testament, from the Leningrad Codex, with its root, its grammar and an English meaning.
works.citation: STEPBible, TAHOT: Translators Amalgamated Hebrew OT. Data created by www.STEPBible.org based on work at Tyndale House Cambridge (CC BY 4.0). github.com/STEPBible/STEPBible-Data. This copy: October 2026.

works.plain: Greek New Testament, word by word
works.title: Translators Amalgamated Greek NT (TAGNT)
works.by: STEPBible.org, based on work at Tyndale House, Cambridge
works.what: Every Greek word of the New Testament in the major printed editions, with its root, its grammar, an English meaning and which editions have it.
works.citation: STEPBible, TAGNT: Translators Amalgamated Greek NT (NA27/28, SBL, Tyndale House, Westcott-Hort, Tregelles, Textus Receptus and Byzantine editions). Data created by www.STEPBible.org based on work at Tyndale House Cambridge (CC BY 4.0). github.com/STEPBible/STEPBible-Data. This copy: October 2026.

works.title: The Peshitta New Testament (Digital Syriac Corpus)
works.by: Digital Syriac Corpus: edition by James E. Walters, Syriac text typed by George A. Kiraz
works.what: The New Testament in Syriac, a dialect of Aramaic, translated from the Greek. The app shows it at Deep beside the English, as a translation and never as Jesus' own words.
works.licenseNote: The digital edition is CC BY 4.0; the Syriac text, printed in 1905, is public domain.

read.label: Digital Syriac Corpus, starting at Matthew

works.citation: The New Testament in Syriac (British and Foreign Bible Society, 1905). Digital Syriac Corpus (syriaccorpus.org): TEI XML edition by James E. Walters, Syriac text transcribed by George A. Kiraz, CC BY 4.0.

works.plain: Word links from Hebrew and Greek to English
works.title: Clear Bible word alignments for the BSB
works.by: Clear Bible (Biblica); the Greek links made by the Berean Bible team, the Hebrew by BiblioNexus
works.what: Links from each Hebrew, Aramaic and Greek word to the words of the BSB that translate it, made by hand. They let the app color matching words.
works.licenseNote: The alignments are CC BY 4.0; the Hebrew (WLC) and BSB texts they link are public domain.
works.citation: Clear Bible / Biblica, Alignments: BSB manual alignments WLCM-BSB and BGNT-BSB, github.com/Clear-Bible/Alignments (CC BY 4.0). This copy: May 2026.

works.plain: Hebrew words with their Greek match
works.title: MACULA Hebrew Linguistic Datasets
works.by: Clear Bible (Biblica)
works.what: Word-by-word data on the Hebrew Old Testament. The app uses one part: for each Hebrew word, the Greek word the Septuagint (the ancient Greek Old Testament) uses there.
works.licenseNote: The data is CC BY 4.0 (Biblica); the Hebrew text it annotates, the Westminster Leningrad Codex, is public domain.
works.citation: MACULA Hebrew Linguistic Datasets, (C) Biblica, Inc., CC BY 4.0, github.com/Clear-Bible/macula-hebrew.

works.title: OpenBible.info Cross References
works.by: OpenBible.info
works.what: About 340,000 pairs of related verses, built mostly from the Treasury of Scripture Knowledge, with readers' votes on how closely each pair is related.
works.citation: OpenBible.info, Cross References (file dated 2024-11-04), https://www.openbible.info/labs/cross-references/ (CC BY 4.0), via the unmodified copy in scrollmapper/bible_databases.

works.title: Easton's Bible Dictionary
works.by: Matthew George Easton
works.what: A Scottish minister's dictionary of the people, places and things of the Bible, first called the Illustrated Bible Dictionary. Written in the 1800s, so some of what it says is out of date.
works.licenseNote: The dictionary is public domain. This copy is the Christian Classics Ethereal Library's transcription, carried by CCEL Paragraphs (CC BY-SA 4.0) and NEUU's Bible Dictionary Dataset (CC BY 4.0).
works.citation: M. G. Easton, Illustrated Bible Dictionary, 3rd ed. (Thomas Nelson, 1897), known as Easton's Bible Dictionary. Text from the Christian Classics Ethereal Library's transcription, via CCEL Paragraphs by Jon Craton (CC BY-SA 4.0) and the Bible Dictionary Dataset, Copyright (c) 2026 NEUU, github.com/neuu-org/bible-dictionary-dataset (CC BY 4.0).

works.title: Smith's Bible Dictionary
works.by: William Smith; this edition revised by F. N. and M. A. Peloubet
works.what: A one-volume American edition of William Smith's Dictionary of the Bible, with notes added by its editors. Written in the 1800s, so some of what it says is out of date.
works.licenseNote: The dictionary is public domain. This copy is the Christian Classics Ethereal Library's transcription, carried by CCEL Paragraphs (CC BY-SA 4.0) and NEUU's Bible Dictionary Dataset (CC BY 4.0).
works.citation: William Smith, Smith's Bible Dictionary, the Christian Classics Ethereal Library's edition, dated 1884: the American edition revised and edited by F. N. and M. A. Peloubet (Philadelphia: Porter & Coates, 1884). First published as A Dictionary of the Bible (London: John Murray, 1860–1863). Text from the Christian Classics Ethereal Library's transcription, via CCEL Paragraphs by Jon Craton (CC BY-SA 4.0) and the Bible Dictionary Dataset, Copyright (c) 2026 NEUU, github.com/neuu-org/bible-dictionary-dataset (CC BY 4.0).

works.title: Nave's Topical Bible
works.by: Orville James Nave
works.what: More than 20,000 subjects, each with the verses that speak of it. Ask the Bible uses it as an index to gather verses, and at Study the Themes tab names its subjects for a verse no theme reaches. Only its headings show, never its entries.
works.licenseNote: The table edition the app reads is CC BY 4.0 (Brady Stephenson, BibleData); Nave's book itself is public domain.
works.citation: Orville J. Nave, Nave's Topical Bible (Lincoln, Nebraska: Topical Bible Publishing Co., 1896–1897). Table edition: Brady Stephenson, BibleData, github.com/BradyStephenson/bible-data (CC BY 4.0).

works.title: Aquifer Open Study Notes
works.by: Bible scholars at Tyndale House Publishers; plain-English adaptation by Mission Mutual
works.what: Short notes on almost every passage of the Bible, explaining people, places, words and background. They show one tap away from a verse, as these scholars' notes.
works.licenseNote: Aquifer Open Study Notes (C) 2026 Mission Mutual, an adaptation of Tyndale Open Study Notes (C) 2023 Tyndale House Publishers, both CC BY-SA 4.0.
works.citation: Aquifer Open Study Notes, (C) 2026 Mission Mutual, CC BY-SA 4.0, github.com/BibleAquifer/AquiferOpenStudyNotes; adapted from Tyndale Open Study Notes, (C) 2023 Tyndale House Publishers, CC BY-SA 4.0, https://tyndaleopenresources.com.

works.plain: Study-Bible notes on the whole Bible
works.title: The Companion Bible
works.by: Printed without a writer's name; generally credited to E. W. Bullinger
works.when: published in six parts; their dates not yet read
works.what: Notes on the King James text marking its figures of speech and the Hebrew and Greek. The edition "is not associated with the name of any man"; the notes are generally credited to E. W. Bullinger (died 1913).
works.citation: The Companion Bible (London: Oxford University Press, in six parts), read on StudyLight (studylight.org/commentaries/eng/bul).

works.title: Reformation Study Bible
works.by: Ligonier Ministries; general editor R. C. Sproul
works.what: Reformed study notes on the whole Bible; each book's notes were written by a scholar named in the printed edition. The app links to them on Bible Gateway.
works.citation: R. C. Sproul, gen. ed., Reformation Study Bible (Ligonier Ministries, 2015), read on Bible Gateway (biblegateway.com/resources/reformation-study-bible).

works.plain: Church Fathers on the Gospels, gathered 1260s
works.title: Catena Aurea (the Golden Chain)
works.by: Thomas Aquinas, from the writings of the Church Fathers; Oxford translation edited by John Henry Newman
works.what: For each passage of the four Gospels, Aquinas linked together what the Church Fathers and later teachers had written on it, each under their name. Shown at Deep, in their own words, once a reader chooses to see them.
works.licenseNote: The Catena Aurea and its Oxford translation are public domain. This copy is from the Catena corpus, whose code is MIT licensed and whose data files mark the text public domain.
works.citation: Thomas Aquinas, Catena Aurea: Commentary on the Four Gospels, Collected out of the Works of the Fathers, Oxford translation edited by John Henry Newman, 4 vols. (Oxford: John Henry Parker; London: J. G. F. and J. Rivington, 1841–45). Text from the Catena corpus, github.com/AlvaroBalbin/catena.

works.plain: Shortened Bible commentary, date not known
works.title: Concise Commentary on the Whole Bible
works.by: An editor not yet identified, abridging Matthew Henry's Commentary and its continuation
works.what: A shortened form of the Bible commentary of Matthew Henry, a Welsh-born Nonconformist minister, which others finished after his death in 1714: a short note on each part of every chapter. Shown at Deep once a reader chooses to see it.
works.licenseNote: Public domain, as the CrossWire SWORD module (MHCC) marks it. This copy is from the Let's Church repository, which is CC0 1.0.
works.citation: Matthew Henry, Concise Commentary on the Whole Bible, from the CrossWire Bible Society's SWORD module MHCC, as kept in the Let's Church repository, github.com/LetsChurch/lets.church (CC0 1.0).

works.title: Explanatory Notes upon the Old and New Testaments
works.by: John Wesley
works.what: Short notes, verse by verse, by the founder of Methodism, written for ordinary readers. Shown at Deep once a reader chooses to see them.
works.licenseNote: Public domain, as the CrossWire SWORD module (Wesley) marks it; based on the electronic edition by Sulu Kelley and Bill Brown. This copy is from the Let's Church repository, which is CC0 1.0.
works.citation: John Wesley, Explanatory Notes upon the New Testament (London, 1755) and Explanatory Notes upon the Old Testament (Bristol, 1765–66), from the CrossWire Bible Society's SWORD module Wesley, as kept in the Let's Church repository, github.com/LetsChurch/lets.church (CC0 1.0).

works.title: Biblical Commentary on the Old Testament
works.by: Carl Friedrich Keil and Franz Delitzsch
works.what: A close, verse by verse commentary on the whole Old Testament by two conservative German Lutheran scholars who held it to be God's word, put into English in Edinburgh. The app links to it on Bible Hub.
works.citation: C. F. Keil and F. Delitzsch, Biblical Commentary on the Old Testament, translated from the German (Edinburgh: T. & T. Clark, 19th century).
cites: C. F. Keil and F. Delitzsch

works.plain: Notes on the New Testament, from 1832
works.title: Notes, Explanatory and Practical, on the New Testament
works.by: Albert Barnes, Presbyterian minister, Philadelphia
works.what: Verse-by-verse notes on the New Testament, written for Sunday-school teachers and Bible classes. Bible Hub shows them as "Barnes' Notes"; the app links there.
works.citation: Albert Barnes, Notes, Explanatory and Practical, on the New Testament (New York, 1832 onward), read on Bible Hub (biblehub.com/commentaries/barnes).

works.plain: Notes on Job, the Psalms, Isaiah and Daniel
works.title: Notes, Critical, Explanatory, and Practical, on Job, the Psalms, Isaiah and Daniel
works.by: Albert Barnes, Presbyterian minister, Philadelphia
works.when: Isaiah 1840; Job 1844; Daniel 1853; the Psalms 1867 (copyright years)
works.what: Albert Barnes's notes on the four Old Testament books he wrote on. On every other Old Testament book, Bible Hub's "Barnes' Notes" are other men's words: see Murphy, Pusey and the Speaker's Commentary.
works.citation: Albert Barnes, Notes, Critical, Explanatory, and Practical, on the Book of the Prophet Isaiah (1840), the Book of Job (1844), the Book of Daniel (1853) and the Book of Psalms (1867 onward), read on Bible Hub (biblehub.com/commentaries/barnes).

works.title: A Critical and Exegetical Commentary on the Book of Genesis, with a New Translation
works.by: James G. Murphy, Presbyterian minister and Professor of Hebrew at the Assembly's College, Belfast
works.when: Andover edition 1866 (the Edinburgh first edition is not yet dated here)
works.what: Bible Hub shows these Genesis notes under “Barnes’ Notes”, but the words are Murphy's: every Genesis comment the app cites is in his printed book.
works.citation: J. G. Murphy, A Critical and Exegetical Commentary on the Book of Genesis, with a New Translation (Andover: Warren F. Draper, 1866), read on Bible Hub (biblehub.com/commentaries/barnes/genesis).

works.plain: Commentary on the Minor Prophets, from 1860
works.title: The Minor Prophets, with a Commentary Explanatory and Practical
works.by: E. B. Pusey, Regius Professor of Hebrew and Canon of Christ Church, Oxford
works.when: published in parts from 1860; London edition 1883 read
works.what: Bible Hub shows these notes on Hosea to Malachi under “Barnes’ Notes”, but the words are Pusey's: every cited comment is in his printed book.
works.citation: E. B. Pusey, The Minor Prophets, with a Commentary Explanatory and Practical (Oxford, from 1860; London: Walter Smith, 1883), read on Bible Hub (biblehub.com/commentaries/barnes).

works.title: The Holy Bible, with an Explanatory and Critical Commentary (the Speaker's Commentary)
works.by: Bishops and other clergy of the Church of England; edited by F. C. Cook, Canon of Exeter
works.when: volumes of 1873 to 1876 read, and 1877 and 1886 printings of vols. I and II
works.what: A commentary on the whole Bible, each book by its own writer. Bible Hub shows its notes on Exodus to the Song of Solomon, Jeremiah and Ezekiel under “Barnes’ Notes”; the writers are listed below.
works.citation: The Holy Bible according to the Authorized Version (A.D. 1611), with an Explanatory and Critical Commentary and a Revision of the Translation, by Bishops and other Clergy of the Anglican Church, edited by F. C. Cook (London: John Murray), read on Bible Hub (biblehub.com/commentaries/barnes).

works.title: Ellicott's Commentary for English Readers
works.by: Various writers, edited by Charles John Ellicott, Bishop of Gloucester and Bristol
works.when: Old Testament 1882 to 1884; New Testament from 1878
works.what: A commentary on the whole Bible for readers without Greek or Hebrew, each book by its own writer. The writers the app cites are listed below; A. S. Aglen's books are no longer cited.
works.citation: Charles John Ellicott, ed., An Old Testament Commentary for English Readers, 5 vols. (London: Cassell, 1882 to 1884), and A New Testament Commentary for English Readers, 3 vols. (from 1878), read on Bible Hub (biblehub.com/commentaries/ellicott).

works.title: The Pulpit Commentary
works.by: Various writers, edited by H. D. M. Spence and Joseph S. Exell
works.what: A commentary on the whole Bible with an exposition, homiletics and homilies for each book. Bible Hub shows only the exposition, whose writers are listed below. Its volume on Jeremiah and Lamentations is not cited.
works.licenseNote: The printed volumes are public domain. Bible Hub's electronic text says "Copyright (c) 2001, 2003, 2005, 2006, 2010 by BibleSoft, inc."; the app links to it and copies none of it.
works.citation: H. D. M. Spence and Joseph S. Exell, eds., The Pulpit Commentary (London: Kegan Paul, Trench and Co., 1880 to 1897), read on Bible Hub (biblehub.com/commentaries/pulpit).

works.title: A Commentary, Critical and Explanatory, on the Old and New Testaments
works.by: Robert Jamieson, A. R. Fausset and David Brown
works.when: New York reprints of 1873 and 1878 of the English edition
works.what: A short commentary on the whole Bible. Its title page divides it: Genesis to Esther by Jamieson, Job to Malachi and 1 Corinthians to Revelation by Fausset, Matthew to Romans by Brown.
works.citation: Robert Jamieson, A. R. Fausset and David Brown, A Commentary, Critical and Explanatory, on the Old and New Testaments (New York: S. S. Scranton, 1873), read on Bible Hub (biblehub.com/commentaries/jfb).

works.title: An Exposition of the Old and New Testament
works.by: Matthew Henry; Romans to Revelation completed after his death by other ministers
works.what: A devotional commentary on the whole Bible. Henry wrote Genesis to Acts; the epistles and Revelation were completed by other ministers, named in the edition's preface.
works.citation: Matthew Henry, An Exposition of the Old and New Testament, edited by George Burder and Joseph Hughes (Philadelphia: Barrington and Haswell, 1828), read on Bible Hub (biblehub.com/commentaries/mhcw).

works.title: Annotations upon the Holy Bible
works.by: Matthew Poole (to Isaiah 58), then other ministers not named in print
works.what: Short notes on the whole Bible. Poole wrote the first volume to Isaiah 58; the second volume is "a Continuation of Mr. Pool's Work by certain Judicious and Learned Divines", not named.
works.citation: Matthew Poole, Annotations upon the Holy Bible, 2 vols. (London, 1683 and 1685), read on Bible Hub (biblehub.com/commentaries/poole).

works.title: An Exposition of the Old and New Testament
works.by: John Gill, English Particular Baptist minister
works.what: A verse-by-verse exposition of the whole Bible, often citing old Jewish writings as witnesses.
works.citation: John Gill, An Exposition of the New Testament and An Exposition of the Old Testament (London, 1746 to 1765), read on Bible Hub (biblehub.com/commentaries/gill).

works.title: The Holy Bible, with a Commentary and Critical Notes
works.by: Adam Clarke, Methodist preacher and scholar
works.what: A commentary on the whole Bible by a Methodist scholar, with notes on the Hebrew and Greek.
works.citation: Adam Clarke, The Holy Bible ... with a Commentary and Critical Notes (London: Butterworth, 1817 printing), read on Bible Hub (biblehub.com/commentaries/clarke).

works.title: The Holy Bible, with Notes, Critical, Explanatory, and Practical
works.by: Joseph Benson, English Methodist minister
works.when: date not yet read from a dated copy
works.what: A commentary on the whole Bible by an early Methodist minister. The app links to it on Bible Hub.
works.citation: Joseph Benson, The Holy Bible ... with Notes, Critical, Explanatory, and Practical, read on Bible Hub (biblehub.com/commentaries/benson).

works.plain: Notes on the New Testament, English 1857
works.title: Gnomon of the New Testament
works.by: J. A. Bengel, Lutheran clergyman and Greek scholar
works.when: English edition from 1857 (Edinburgh: T. and T. Clark)
works.what: Brief notes on the Greek words of the New Testament, in the English translation published in Edinburgh. John Wesley drew on them for his own notes.
works.citation: J. A. Bengel, Gnomon of the New Testament, English translation (Edinburgh: T. and T. Clark, from 1857), read on Bible Hub (biblehub.com/commentaries/bengel).

works.title: Commentaries
works.by: John Calvin, Reformer and pastor in Geneva
works.what: Calvin's commentaries on most books of the Bible, in the English translation of the Calvin Translation Society. The app links to them on Bible Hub.

read.label: archive.org, the Minor Prophets, vol. I

works.citation: John Calvin, Commentaries, translated for the Calvin Translation Society (Edinburgh, from 1844), read on Bible Hub (biblehub.com/commentaries/calvin).

works.title: Expositions of Holy Scripture
works.by: Alexander Maclaren, Scottish Baptist minister
works.what: Expository sermons on passages through the whole Bible.
works.citation: Alexander Maclaren, Expositions of Holy Scripture (London: Hodder and Stoughton, 1906 printing), read on Bible Hub (biblehub.com/commentaries/maclaren).

works.title: The Treasury of David
works.by: C. H. Spurgeon, English Particular Baptist preacher
works.what: Spurgeon's exposition of the Psalms, with notes gathered from other writers.
works.citation: C. H. Spurgeon, The Treasury of David, vol. V (1878), read on Bible Hub (biblehub.com/commentaries/tod).

works.plain: Study notes of the Geneva Bible, 1599
works.title: The Geneva Bible notes
works.by: English Protestant exiles at Geneva; Laurence Tomson (New Testament); Franciscus Junius (Revelation)
works.what: The study notes printed in the Geneva Bible, read by the Puritans. The Old Testament notes are the exiles'; the New Testament notes are Tomson's, after Beza, and those on Revelation are Junius's.
works.citation: The Geneva Bible notes, 1599 edition, read on Bible Hub (biblehub.com/commentaries/gsb).

works.title: Figures of Speech Used in the Bible, Explained and Illustrated
works.by: E. W. Bullinger, Anglican clergyman
works.what: A catalogue of the figures of speech used in the Bible, plays on words included, each with verses that show it.
works.citation: E. W. Bullinger, Figures of Speech Used in the Bible, Explained and Illustrated (London: Eyre and Spottiswoode, 1898).

works.plain: Writings of the early church, in translation
works.title: The church fathers, as New Advent gives them
works.by: Justin Martyr, Irenaeus, Clement of Rome, Gregory of Nazianzus, Jerome, Athanasius, Augustine, John Chrysostom, and the unknown writer of the Epistle of Barnabas
works.when: first to fifth centuries; English translations of 1885 to 1896
works.what: Early Christian writings the Layers notes cite, each in the English of the Ante-Nicene and Nicene and Post-Nicene Fathers. Each cite names the writer, the work and its translator.
works.citation: The Ante-Nicene Fathers (1885 to 1896) and the Nicene and Post-Nicene Fathers (1888 to 1894), read on New Advent (newadvent.org/fathers), revised and edited there by Kevin Knight.

works.title: The Life and Times of Jesus the Messiah
works.by: Alfred Edersheim, Jewish-born Christian biblical scholar
works.what: A life of Jesus set against the Jewish world of his day.

works.title: Tyndale Open Bible Dictionary
works.by: Tyndale House Publishers; edited by Philip W. Comfort and Walter A. Elwell
works.what: A modern Bible dictionary that Tyndale shares under an open license. The app quotes its articles word for word for when each part of the Bible happened and when each book was written.
works.citation: Tyndale Open Bible Dictionary, ed. Philip W. Comfort and Walter A. Elwell. Copyright (C) 2023 by Tyndale House Publishers. Licensed under CC BY-SA 4.0. Available free at http://www.tyndaleopenresources.com.

works.by: STEPBible.org, based on work at Tyndale House, Cambridge
works.what: Short definitions for every Hebrew and Aramaic word root of the Old Testament, abridged from the Brown-Driver-Briggs lexicon of 1906.
works.citation: STEPBible, TBESH: Translators Brief lexicon of Extended Strongs for Hebrew, based on the Abridged BDB (Online Bible). Data created by www.STEPBible.org based on work at Tyndale House Cambridge (CC BY 4.0). github.com/STEPBible/STEPBible-Data. This copy: October 2026.

works.plain: Greek word list, from a 1922 dictionary
works.title: Translators Brief lexicon of Extended Strongs for Greek (TBESG)
works.by: STEPBible.org, based on work at Tyndale House, Cambridge
works.what: Short definitions for every Greek word root of the New Testament, mostly from Abbott-Smith's lexicon of 1922.
works.citation: STEPBible, TBESG: Translators Brief lexicon of Extended Strongs for Greek, based on the definitions of G. Abbott-Smith. Data created by www.STEPBible.org based on work at Tyndale House Cambridge (CC BY 4.0). github.com/STEPBible/STEPBible-Data. This copy: October 2026.

works.title: Liddell-Scott-Jones Greek-English Lexicon (STEPBible TFLSJ)
works.by: Henry George Liddell, Robert Scott, Henry Stuart Jones and Roderick McKenzie; put online by the Perseus Digital Library; formatted and dated by STEPBible
works.what: The great dictionary of ancient Greek, from Homer on. The app uses only its short meanings and the century of the earliest writer it cites for each.
works.licenseNote: The LSJ text from the Perseus Digital Library is CC BY-SA 4.0; STEPBible's formatting and dates are CC BY 4.0.
works.citation: H. G. Liddell, R. Scott, H. S. Jones and R. McKenzie, A Greek-English Lexicon, 9th ed. (Oxford University Press, 1940), from the Perseus Digital Library, Tufts University (CC BY-SA 4.0); formatted, with dates added to authors, as STEPBible TFLSJ: Translators Formatted full LSJ Bible lexicon. Data created by www.STEPBible.org based on work at Tyndale House Cambridge (CC BY 4.0). github.com/STEPBible/STEPBible-Data.

works.title: Strong's Hebrew and Greek dictionaries
works.by: James Strong; JSON edition by Open Scriptures (Greek from Ulrik Petersen's XML, Hebrew edited by David Troidl)
works.what: The short dictionaries in Strong's Exhaustive Concordance, which gave every Hebrew and Greek word a number. The app uses only their notes on which word comes from which, for each word's family.
works.licenseNote: Strong's dictionaries are public domain; the JSON edition by Open Scriptures is CC BY-SA.
works.citation: James Strong, A Concise Dictionary of the Words in the Hebrew Bible and Dictionary of Greek Words, from The Exhaustive Concordance of the Bible (1890). JSON edition: Open Scriptures, github.com/openscriptures/strongs (CC BY-SA). This copy: October 2026.

works.title: A Greek-English Lexicon of the New Testament
works.by: Joseph Henry Thayer, from the Latin lexicon of C. L. W. Grimm and C. G. Wilke
works.what: A classic dictionary of New Testament Greek, translated and enlarged by an American scholar. Old, but still widely used.
works.citation: Joseph Henry Thayer, A Greek-English Lexicon of the New Testament, being Grimm's Wilke's Clavis Novi Testamenti, translated, revised and enlarged (New York: American Book Company, 1889).

works.title: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
works.by: George Abbott-Smith
works.what: A compact dictionary of New Testament Greek that also notes how the Greek Old Testament uses many of its words. STEPBible's short Greek definitions come mostly from it.
works.citation: G. Abbott-Smith, A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament (Edinburgh: T. & T. Clark, 1922).
cites: G. Abbott-Smith, A Manual Greek Lexicon

works.title: OpenBible.info Bible Geocoding Data
works.by: OpenBible.info
works.what: Every place the Bible names that can be located, the modern sites proposed for it and how sure each one is, with the sources behind them, and the shapes of regions such as Galilee and Edom.
works.licenseNote: Coordinates the dataset takes from OpenStreetMap or Google are left out of the app.
works.citation: OpenBible.info, Bible Geocoding Data (2021), https://www.openbible.info/geo/, github.com/openbibleinfo/Bible-Geocoding-Data (CC BY 4.0).

works.plain: Data on Bible people and places
works.title: Theographic Bible Metadata
works.by: Robert Rouse (viz.bible)
works.what: Linked lists of the people, places and events of the Bible. The app uses it to name who was born, died or was present at each place.
works.licenseNote: The people file the app builds from it is shared under the same license.
works.citation: Robert Rouse, Theographic Bible Metadata (viz.bible), github.com/robertrouse/theographic-bible-metadata (CC BY-SA 4.0). This copy: April 2026.

works.title: Natural Earth
works.by: Natural Earth: Tom Patterson, Nathaniel Vaughn Kelso and others
works.what: Free map data of the whole world. The app uses its coastlines, lakes, rivers, sea names and today's borders for the Places map.
works.citation: Made with Natural Earth. Free vector and raster map data @ naturalearthdata.com. Version 5.2.0-pre, via github.com/nvkelso/natural-earth-vector.

works.title: The Mishnah
works.by: Rabbi Judah the Prince, from the teachings of earlier rabbis
works.what: The first great written collection of Jewish law and teaching, mostly in Hebrew. The app cites it for words that also appear in the Gospels.
works.licenseNote: The Hebrew text is public domain; Sefaria's English translations carry their own licenses.
works.citation: The Mishnah, compiled by Rabbi Judah ha-Nasi, late 2nd or early 3rd century AD. Cited by tractate, chapter and paragraph (Avot, Taanit).

works.plain: Book defending the Jews, after AD 94
works.title: Against Apion
works.by: Flavius Josephus
works.what: A Jewish historian's answer, in Greek, to attacks on the Jewish people. It quotes older Greek writers who mention the Jews and their customs.
works.licenseNote: William Whiston's English translation (1737) is public domain.
works.citation: Flavius Josephus, Against Apion (Greek, after AD 94), cited by book and section; English translation by William Whiston.

works.title: Jewish Antiquities
works.by: Flavius Josephus
works.what: A history of the Jewish people in twenty books, written in Greek, from the creation to the war with Rome that began in AD 66.
works.licenseNote: William Whiston's English translation (1737) is public domain.
works.citation: Flavius Josephus, Jewish Antiquities (Greek, AD 94), cited by book and section; English translation by William Whiston.

works.plain: Jewish commentary on Genesis, 1st century AD
works.title: Allegorical Interpretation
works.by: Philo of Alexandria
works.what: A Jewish thinker's commentary, in Greek, on passages of Genesis, read as pictures of the soul. It explains names such as Melchizedek and Salem.
works.licenseNote: C. D. Yonge's English translation (1854–55) is public domain.
works.citation: Philo of Alexandria, Allegorical Interpretation (Legum allegoriae), cited by book and section. English translation: "On the Allegories of the Sacred Laws", in The Works of Philo Judaeus, translated by C. D. Yonge, vol. 1 (London: Bohn, 1854).

works.title: The Didache (The Teaching of the Twelve Apostles)
works.by: Unknown early Christians
works.when: 1st century AD, as most scholars date it
works.what: A short early Christian guide to how to live, baptize and share the Lord's Supper, written in Greek. One of its prayers keeps the Aramaic word Maranatha.
works.citation: The Didache, or Teaching of the Twelve Apostles (Greek, 1st century AD), cited by chapter and verse. Known from a Greek manuscript of 1056 published by Philotheos Bryennios in 1883. English translation in J. B. Lightfoot, The Apostolic Fathers.

works.title: 4 Ezra (2 Esdras 3–14)
works.by: An unknown Jewish writer, in Ezra's name
works.what: Visions written in Ezra's name after Jerusalem fell in AD 70, kept in Latin and other translations. Some Bibles print it among the Apocrypha as 2 Esdras.
works.licenseNote: G. H. Box's English translation (1917) is public domain in the United States.
works.citation: 4 Ezra (2 Esdras 3–14), late 1st century AD. English translation: G. H. Box, The Apocalypse of Ezra (II Esdras iii–xiv), Translated from the Syriac (London: SPCK, 1917). Verses 7:36–105, missing from most Latin copies, were published by R. L. Bensly in 1875.

works.title: Targum of Psalms
works.by: Unknown Jewish translators
works.when: date unknown; the oldest dated copy is from 1237–1238
works.what: An Aramaic rendering of the Psalms made for Jewish readers. At Psalm 22 its words are close to Jesus' cry from the cross.
works.citation: Targum of Psalms (Aramaic), text of the Mikraot Gedolot as given by Sefaria (public domain). Its date is uncertain; the oldest dated manuscript is the Breslau manuscript of 1237–1238.

works.plain: Edition of a Dead Sea Scroll, 1962
works.title: The Copper Scroll (3Q15), in Discoveries in the Judaean Desert III
works.by: Unknown; edited by J. T. Milik, with R. de Vaux and H. W. Baker
works.what: A list of hidden treasure engraved on copper, found in a cave near Qumran in 1952. The app cites it for a place name often linked with the pool of Bethesda.
works.licenseNote: The scroll is ancient; the 1962 edition that publishes it is under copyright.
works.citation: J. T. Milik, "Le rouleau de cuivre provenant de la grotte 3Q (3Q15)", with R. de Vaux and H. W. Baker, in M. Baillet, J. T. Milik and R. de Vaux, Les 'Petites Grottes' de Qumrân, Discoveries in the Judaean Desert of Jordan III (Oxford: Clarendon Press, 1962), 201–302.

works.title: A Textual Commentary on the Greek New Testament
works.by: Bruce M. Metzger
works.what: Explains, passage by passage, why the editors of the standard Greek New Testament chose one wording where old copies differ.
works.citation: Bruce M. Metzger, A Textual Commentary on the Greek New Testament, 2nd ed. (Stuttgart: Deutsche Bibelgesellschaft / German Bible Society, 1994).
cites: Bruce M. Metzger, A Textual Commentary

works.title: ΒΑΡΝΑΒΑΣ: ϒΙΟΣ ΠΑΡΑΚΛΗΣΕΩΣ
works.by: Sebastian Brock
works.what: On the name Barnabas, and why Acts 4:36 explains it as Son of Encouragement.
works.citation: Sebastian Brock, "ΒΑΡΝΑΒΑΣ: ϒΙΟΣ ΠΑΡΑΚΛΗΣΕΩΣ", Journal of Theological Studies n.s. 25.1 (1974): 93–98, https://doi.org/10.1093/jts/XXV.1.93.

works.plain: Article on the words for Hebrew, 2019
works.title: Ancient Names for Hebrew and Aramaic: A Case for Lexical Revision
works.by: Ken M. Penner
works.what: Argues that the Greek word for "in Hebrew" means Hebrew, not Aramaic, and that dictionaries should say so.
works.citation: Ken M. Penner, "Ancient Names for Hebrew and Aramaic: A Case for Lexical Revision", New Testament Studies 65.3 (2019): 412–423, https://doi.org/10.1017/S0028688519000067.

works.plain: Chapter on the words for Hebrew, 2014
works.title: Hebraisti in Ancient Texts: Does Ἑβραϊστί Ever Mean 'Aramaic'?
works.by: Randall Buth and Chad Pierce
works.what: Looks at how ancient texts use the Greek word for "in Hebrew" and asks whether it ever means Aramaic.
works.citation: Randall Buth and Chad Pierce, "Hebraisti in Ancient Texts: Does Ἑβραϊστί Ever Mean 'Aramaic'?", in Randall Buth and R. Steven Notley (eds.), The Language Environment of First Century Judaea, Jerusalem Studies in the Synoptic Gospels 2 (Leiden: Brill, 2014), chapter 3.

works.plain: Chapter on Jesus' cry from the cross, 2014
works.title: The Riddle of Jesus' Cry from the Cross
works.by: Randall Buth
works.what: Asks why Matthew and Mark give Jesus' cry from the cross in different forms, Eli and Eloi, and what each one tells the reader.
works.citation: Randall Buth, "The Riddle of Jesus' Cry from the Cross: The Meaning of ηλι ηλι λαμα σαβαχθανι (Matthew 27:46) and the Literary Function of ελωι ελωι λειμα σαβαχθανι (Mark 15:34)", in Randall Buth and R. Steven Notley (eds.), The Language Environment of First Century Judaea, Jerusalem Studies in the Synoptic Gospels 2 (Leiden: Brill, 2014), chapter 11.

works.plain: Book on the words of Jesus, 1902
works.title: The Words of Jesus
works.by: Gustaf Dalman; translated by D. M. Kay
works.what: A German scholar of Aramaic studies Jesus' sayings in the light of later Jewish writings and the Aramaic language.
works.citation: Gustaf Dalman, The Words of Jesus Considered in the Light of Post-Biblical Jewish Writings and the Aramaic Language, English translation by D. M. Kay (Edinburgh: T. & T. Clark, 1902).
cites: Gustaf Dalman, The Words of Jesus

works.title: Grammatik des jüdisch-palästinischen Aramäisch
works.by: Gustaf Dalman
works.what: A grammar, in German, of the Aramaic of Jewish writings from the land of Israel, such as the Jerusalem Talmud and the Targums.
works.citation: Gustaf Dalman, Grammatik des jüdisch-palästinischen Aramäisch nach den Idiomen des palästinischen Talmud und Midrasch, des Onkelostargum (Cod. Socini 84) und der jerusalemischen Targume zum Pentateuch, 2nd ed. (Leipzig: Hinrichs, 1905).

works.plain: Articles in an evangelical journal, 1989 to 2023
works.title: Themelios
works.by: The Gospel Coalition's journal; articles by Torleif Elgvin, Jey J. Kanagaraj, David L. Baker, Walter Riggans, R. T. France, Matt Champlin, Bruce Reichenbach and David V. Christensen
works.what: An international evangelical journal for students of theology. The app cites the articles named here, each linked.
works.citation: Themelios (The Gospel Coalition), thegospelcoalition.org/themelios.

works.title: Journal of the Evangelical Theological Society
works.by: The Evangelical Theological Society; articles by Herbert W. Bateman IV, Paul M. Hoskins, Gary Yates, Gregory R. Lanier and Jeannine K. Brown
works.what: The journal of a society whose members affirm that the Bible is without error. The app cites the articles named here, each linked.
works.citation: Journal of the Evangelical Theological Society, etsjets.org/JETS.

works.title: Eden, the Temple, and the Church's Mission in the New Creation
works.by: G. K. Beale, Reformed New Testament scholar
works.what: An article in the Journal of the Evangelical Theological Society 48/1 on the garden and the temple, from Genesis to Revelation 21 and 22.
works.citation: G. K. Beale, "Eden, the Temple, and the Church's Mission in the New Creation," Journal of the Evangelical Theological Society 48/1 (2005): 5-31.

works.plain: Two essays on Jesus and Paul
works.title: Essays by F. F. Bruce
works.by: F. F. Bruce, evangelical scholar
works.when: 1982 (the Son of Man essay); the year of the other is not printed in the copy read
works.what: The Background to the Son of Man Sayings (in Christ the Lord) and The Curse of the Law (in Paul and Paulinism).
works.citation: F. F. Bruce, "The Background to the Son of Man Sayings," in H. H. Rowdon, ed., Christ the Lord (Leicester: Inter-Varsity Press, 1982), 50-70; "The Curse of the Law," in M. D. Hooker and S. G. Wilson, eds., Paul and Paulinism (London: SPCK), 27-36.

works.title: Recent Translations of Genesis 3:15
works.by: M. H. Woudstra, Old Testament scholar, Calvin Theological Seminary
works.what: An article in the Calvin Theological Journal 6 on how Genesis 3:15 is translated.
works.citation: M. H. Woudstra, "Recent Translations of Genesis 3:15," Calvin Theological Journal 6 (1971): 194-203.

works.title: Essays at the Theopolis Institute
works.by: Peter J. Leithart, President of the Theopolis Institute
works.what: Short essays by a Reformed theologian on reading the Bible: Firstborn (2011) and What's in a Name? (2014).
works.citation: Peter J. Leithart, "Firstborn" (2011) and "What's in a Name?" (2014), Theopolis Institute, theopolisinstitute.com.

works.title: Bible Backgrounds
works.by: Craig S. Keener, New Testament scholar, Asbury Theological Seminary
works.what: Short articles on the setting of passages in Genesis.
works.citation: Craig S. Keener, "Jacob gets Esau's blessing" and "Sleeping with a prostitute part 2" (2016), Bible Backgrounds, craigkeener.com.

works.title: Maranatha and the Identity of Jesus
works.by: Michael F. Bird, evangelical Anglican scholar
works.what: An article on the Aramaic prayer in 1 Corinthians 16:22.
works.citation: Michael F. Bird, "Maranatha and the Identity of Jesus," Word from the Bird (2024), michaelfbird.substack.com.

works.title: One God, One Lord (Part 8)
works.by: David B. Capes, Baptist New Testament scholar
works.what: An article on 1 Corinthians 16:22 and early worship of Jesus.
works.citation: David B. Capes, "One God, One Lord (Part 8)," A Word in Edgewise (2020), davidbcapes.com.

works.title: GotQuestions.org
works.by: Got Questions Ministries; founded by S. Michael Houdmann
works.what: Short answers to questions about the Bible and faith, from an evangelical, nondenominational ministry. The articles are unsigned, written by staff and volunteers who hold its statement of faith.
works.citation: GotQuestions.org. Got Questions Ministries, 2002–. https://www.gotquestions.org/.

works.plain: Articles by pastors and scholars, since 2005
works.title: The Gospel Coalition
works.by: The Gospel Coalition, Inc.; founded by D. A. Carson and Timothy Keller
works.what: Articles, podcasts and books by many named pastors and scholars, from a fellowship of evangelical churches in the Reformed tradition. It also publishes the journal Themelios.
works.citation: The Gospel Coalition. The Gospel Coalition, Inc., 2007–. https://www.thegospelcoalition.org/.

works.title: Bible.org
works.by: Biblical Studies Foundation
works.what: Over 20,000 articles, Bible studies and sermons by named pastors and scholars, from a broadly evangelical, nondenominational ministry. It is also the home of the NET Bible.
works.citation: Bible.org. Biblical Studies Foundation, 1994–. https://bible.org/.

works.title: Catholic Answers
works.by: Catholic Answers, Inc.; founded by Karl Keating
works.what: Answers to questions about the Catholic faith: articles, an encyclopedia, a magazine and a radio show. A lay-run ministry in good standing with the Diocese of San Diego, though not an official body of the Church.
works.citation: Catholic Answers. Catholic Answers, Inc., 1979–. https://www.catholic.com/.

works.plain: Teaching ministry of R.C. Sproul, since 1971
works.title: Ligonier Ministries
works.by: Ligonier Ministries; founded by R.C. Sproul
works.what: Articles, the magazine Tabletalk, teaching videos and podcasts, much of it R.C. Sproul's, from a Reformed Protestant teaching ministry that holds the historic Reformed confessions.
works.citation: Ligonier Ministries. Ligonier Ministries, Inc., 1971–. https://www.ligonier.org/.

works.title: Christianity Today
works.by: Christianity Today International; founded by Billy Graham
works.what: A magazine and website of news, essays and reviews by its editors and outside writers, begun by Billy Graham with Carl F. H. Henry as its first editor. Evangelical, and tied to no denomination.
works.citation: Christianity Today. Christianity Today International, 1956–. https://www.christianitytoday.com/.

works.title: BibleProject
works.by: BibleProject; founded by Tim Mackie and Jon Collins
works.what: Free animated videos, podcasts and classes on each book and theme of the Bible, made by its own team. It belongs to no denomination; its leaders hold the historic orthodox Christian confession.
works.citation: BibleProject. BibleProject, 2014–. https://bibleproject.com/.

works.plain: Teaching ministry of John Piper, since 1994
works.title: Desiring God
works.by: Desiring God Ministries; founded by John Piper
works.what: Articles, sermons, books and podcasts by John Piper and other writers. Its statement of faith is Reformed and Baptist in its teaching, though the ministry names no denomination.
works.citation: Desiring God. Desiring God Ministries, 1994–. https://www.desiringgod.org/.

works.plain: Free Bible and seminary classes, since 2000
works.title: BiblicalTraining.org
works.by: BiblicalTraining.org; founded by Bill Mounce
works.what: Free recorded classes, from the basics to seminary level, taught by professors from many evangelical traditions, from Calvinist to Wesleyan. It calls itself broadly evangelical.
works.citation: BiblicalTraining.org. BiblicalTraining.org, 2000–. https://www.biblicaltraining.org/.

works.plain: Reasons for the Christian faith, since 2006
works.title: CrossExamined.org
works.by: CrossExamined.org; founded by Frank Turek
works.what: Articles, podcasts and talks giving reasons for the Christian faith, mostly by Frank Turek. It calls itself evangelical and inter-denominational, and holds to the Apostles' Creed.
works.citation: CrossExamined.org. CrossExamined.org, 2006–. https://crossexamined.org/.

works.title: Answers in Genesis
works.by: Answers in Genesis; founded by Ken Ham
works.what: Articles and answers defending the Bible's history from Genesis on, from a ministry in Kentucky that also runs the Creation Museum and the Ark Encounter. It holds the Bible to be without error and reads creation as six ordinary days.
works.citation: Answers in Genesis. Answers in Genesis, 1994–. https://answersingenesis.org/.

works.title: OrthodoxWiki
works.by: Its volunteer editors
works.what: A wiki encyclopedia of Eastern Orthodox Christianity, written by registered volunteer editors. It says it is not an official voice of Orthodoxy.
works.licenseNote: Most pages are shared under CC BY-SA 2.5 or the GNU Free Documentation License; older edits and pages taken from Wikipedia have other terms. The app only links to it.
works.citation: OrthodoxWiki. 2004–. https://orthodoxwiki.org/.

works.title: BibleRef.com
works.by: Got Questions Ministries
works.what: Plain explanations of what a verse means, written verse by verse, from the same evangelical ministry as GotQuestions.org. So far it covers the New Testament and parts of the Old.
works.citation: BibleRef.com. Got Questions Ministries. https://www.bibleref.com/.

works.title: Bible Hub
works.by: the Online Parallel Bible Project
works.what: A large free Bible study site with many older commentaries. The app links to two believing ones, chapter by chapter: Jamieson, Fausset and Brown (1871) on the whole Bible, and Keil and Delitzsch on the Old Testament.
works.citation: Bible Hub. Online Parallel Bible Project, 2004–. https://biblehub.com/.

works.title: potion-base-8M (Model2Vec)
works.by: Minish Lab: Stephan Tulkens and Thomas van Dongen
works.what: A small model that gives each English word piece a direction, so words that mean alike point alike. Ask the Bible uses it only to tell which prepared question someone means; every answer is still the Bible's own verses.
works.licenseNote: MIT License, as its model card states. The app keeps every word piece's vector, each number rounded to one of 15 levels. Minish Lab distilled it from BAAI's bge-base-en-v1.5 (MIT) with passages of the C4 web corpus (ODC-BY); no text of either is used here.
works.citation: Stephan Tulkens and Thomas van Dongen, Model2Vec: Fast State-of-the-Art Static Embeddings (Minish Lab, 2024), https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.17270888; model potion-base-8M, https://huggingface.co/minishlab/potion-base-8M (revision bf8b056651a2c21b8d2565580b8569da283cab23, copied from Hugging Face on 20 October 2026), MIT License.
